To understand what a distributed denial of service attack is, it is important to know that attackers often use a network of compromised devices, known as a botnet, to send excessive requests or packets to a target. Application Layer Attacks Application layer DDoS attacks, also known as Layer 7 attacks, target specific applications and services, such as web servers. HTTP floods and Slowloris attacks are common examples. They attempt to exhaust application resources by generating excessive requests or keeping connections open for extended periods. Although these attacks may use less traffic than volumetric attacks, they can still disrupt services by consuming server resources. Attack activity is often measured in requests per second (rps). SQL injection is a separate application-layer attack and should not be classified as a DDoS attack. Common methods used in DDoS attacks include UDP floods, SYN floods, ICMP floods, HTTP floods, and DNS amplification attacks. While UDP and ICMP floods generate large volumes of packets, SYN floods target TCP connection handling, and HTTP floods overwhelm web applications with excessive requests. DNS amplification uses reflection techniques to direct amplified traffic toward a target. Attackers may combine multiple methods to disrupt network infrastructure and applications simultaneously.
